summary.text: A 55-year-old man with a history of hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus, taking metoprolol for hypertension, was transferred with sudden chest pain. In the emergency room he was pale, diaphoretic and hemodynamically unstable, with a heart rate of 62 beats/min and blood pressure of 76/48 mm Hg and no limb blood pressure difference.

Electrocardiography showed normal sinus rhythm with mild ST elevation in V1 and depression in V3-V6, and chest X-ray showed an increased cardiac silhouette. Transthoracic echocardiography indicated ascending aortic dissection with sinus of Valsalva involvement and cardiac tamponade, and he was referred for urgent surgery.

Intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography revealed a large aneurysm adjacent to the left atrium that arose between the mitral and aortic valve annuli, with systolic flow from the left ventricle, plus a calcified bicuspid aortic valve. He was diagnosed with a bicuspid aortic valve and a ruptured left ventricular aneurysm with cardiac tamponade, a true aneurysm, missed on preoperative TTE.

During surgery the tamponade was relieved, the aneurysmal orifice was closed with a patch, and the aortic valve was replaced with a mechanical valve; no ascending aortic dissection was identified. Postoperative TEE showed no connection between the left ventricle and the aneurysm, he made an uneventful recovery, and he was later discharged in satisfactory condition.
